summary: Alibaba launches a closed flagship AI model, China readies its first mission with a foreign astronaut, Canada reviews Chinese EVs, and Chinese shoppers keep holding back.
body: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max this week, its most powerful AI model so far. It can read text, images and video, and Alibaba says it cuts the average cost of a task by about 60% compared with its previous top model; its benchmark scores are the company's own claims.[^1][^2] Unlike many earlier Qwen models, it is not open-weight, meaning outside developers cannot download and run it themselves. Alibaba says it filtered training data to remove material that could help cyberattacks.[^1][^2]

In space, the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft was moved to its launch pad at Jiuquan in the Gobi Desert. It will carry the first foreign astronaut to China's Tiangong space station, a Pakistani payload specialist who will stay a few days.[^3][^4] Pakistan's planning minister has named Nov 25 as the launch date; China's space agency says only "at an appropriate time".[^3]

For Canadians, Transport Minister Steve MacKinnon says Ottawa will review where Chinese-made EVs may drive, possibly keeping them away from military and government sites, after Canada cut its tariff on them to 6.1% in January.[^5] Xiaomi opened its first car sales outside China, in the UAE, at prices well above those at home.[^6]

Shoppers in China stayed cautious: retail sales rose only 0.4% in October from a year earlier, with car sales down 21.4%.[^7][^9] New home prices fell 2.4% from a year earlier, the slowest drop in almost a year by Reuters' count.[^8] My read: the property slump is easing, but people are still holding back on big purchases.
differences: Alibaba says Qwen4-Max beats some rival models on its own tests, but The Next Web notes those results have not been independently checked and the model trails on others.[^2] Pakistan names Nov 25 for the launch; China has not given a date.[^3]
